best_for: ReleaseRun sets ordered steps as Swiss columns under one water line: a huge light numeral per step, a node where each step starts, and the last step as the navy column where the water is released.

instances.h: From first call to water you can use

block.h: From first call to water you can use
block.intro: Five steps. Each says what you send or decide.

items.d: You send what you make and where you sell it. We return the water each product needs, so you know if you need this.
You send roughly how much water you use a day, and your water report. We return a package size and budget range.
You agree a short user requirement specification (URS) and the proposal, so both sides sign the same scope.
We build the package and test it in our shop, then test it again on your site.
We run the qualification tests with you. Your quality person then approves the water for use.

block.intro: Four steps, from your purchase order to the start of the lead-time clock. Our bank details never change by email: call [sales phone number] before acting on such a request.

items.d: Make the purchase order (PO) out to [legal entity name]. Quote our proposal number, so price and scope carry over.
Public buyers: add your PO, tender and project numbers. We repeat them on every invoice.
Within [order confirmation time, working days]: order accepted, drawing schedule and one named contact.
Lead time counts from your order and from approved drawings, as page one states.
